svg.title: Roof valleys: open metal valley and closed-cut valley
svg.desc: Two ways to build a valley where two roof slopes meet. Left: an open valley, with ice and water shield under a metal valley liner; the shingles on both sides are cut back so the metal shows, narrowest at the top and widening toward the eave. Right: a closed-cut valley, with ice and water shield centred in the valley; the shingles from one slope run across the valley, and the shingles from the other slope are cut in a straight line 2 inches back from the valley centre, with no nails within 6 inches of the centre. A fully woven valley is not one of the methods the GAF or TAMKO instructions show for these laminated shingles, so NBD does not weave valleys. Illustration, not a photo of an actual job. Layer thicknesses are exaggerated so each one can be seen.
svg.text: Where two slopes meet, the water doubles.
